# html2mp4

> CLI that renders an HTML animation (CSS keyframes/transitions, Web Animations, GSAP, Canvas, Three.js, SVG SMIL) to MP4, WebM or GIF, deterministically, frame by frame, with no changes to the page. Headless Chrome with virtual time; frames piped to ffmpeg. Includes QC checks for the finished video.

Requirements: Node 22.12+, Chrome or Chromium, ffmpeg. `npx html2mp4 doctor` reports what it found.

## Commands

- `npx html2mp4 render <page.html|folder|url> -o out.mp4 [--preset vertical|landscape|square|portrait] [--size WxH] [--duration s] [--fps n] [--audio file] [--qc] [--json]`
- `npx html2mp4 snap <page> --at 0,1.5,3 --sheet sheet.png` writes stills and one contact sheet
- `npx html2mp4 check <video.mp4> [--sheet sheet.png] [--transcode]` gates: format, first frame not blank, longest frozen stretch, loudness/true peak, SSIM after a platform-like re-encode
- `npx html2mp4 render <page> --check-determinism` renders twice and compares every frame
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 a check failed

## Page contract (all optional)

- Size/length: `<meta name="html2mp4" content="size=1080x1920; duration=12; fps=30">` or `window.__render = { width, height, duration, fps }`. Without them: 1920x1080, 30 fps, duration = end of the finite CSS/GSAP animations + 0.5 s.
- Virtual time covers requestAnimationFrame, performance.now, Date, setTimeout/setInterval, requestIdleCallback, CSS animations/transitions, element.animate(), SVG SMIL. Math.random is seeded (`--seed`).
- Seek mode: `window.__render = { duration, seek: async (t) => {} }` (t in seconds, must be a pure function of t) renders in parallel with `--workers`.
- `--wait-for "<js expression>"`: the video starts at the first frame where it is true.

## Rules for pages

- Lay out at the final pixel size (body width/height = video size, px units).
- Make frame 0 a complete composition; hold the end state 0.5-1 s.
- Load fonts and images up front; no mid-animation fetches.
- No `<video>`/`<audio>` timing (pass sound with `--audio`), no iframes or Web Workers for animation, no busy-waiting on performance.now().
